subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — dedicated capacity sizing / pricing

Thanks for the call this morning, Alex — good sync. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size a dedicated capacity proposal that aligns with Finlytics' unit economics and SLA needs. Please confirm or correct any numbers below.

Summary of what I heard:
- Steady-state monthly token volume: ~250M–400M tokens/month (you said 250M is a safe baseline; finance is planning for 300M).
- Peak concurrency: up to ~6k tokens/sec during batch/reporting windows; typical sustained average is closer to ~100 tokens/sec.
- Average generation size: ~120 tokens per request (mix of short replies and longer reports).
- Models: primarily a 13B class model for most traffic; occasional 70B-class for high-quality reporting use-cases.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 500ms for 13B workloads.
- Target unit economics: Finlytics is targeting approximately $65 / 1M tokens (target for budgeting).
- Budget range: internal guidance is $30k–$50k/month for inference spend to start, with potential to commit to a 12-month reserved term if pricing is favorable.

Sizing / options we plan to price (we'll provide concrete line items once you confirm):
A) H100-focused reserved pool (preferred for 70B support) — e.g., 2x H100-80GB nodes to cover peaks with autoscale/burst; expected to comfortably support the occasional 70B runs and sustained mixed traffic.
B) A100 reserve (cost-lever) — e.g., 4x A100-80GB nodes that are strong for 13B workloads and cheaper for sustained 13B-only traffic but may require routing 70B to hosted fallbacks.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm monthly token target (baseline vs ramp) and whether 12-month commit is possible for a better unit price?
2) Please loop in procurement contact (I included procurement@finlytics.com in the follow-up).
3) Would you share a small sample workload (1–2 representative requests with expected response lengths) so we can run early perf estimates?
4) Are you open to a short technical sizing call with Marcus (cc'd) — he can walk through GPU throughput tradeoffs and exact throughput numbers we expect per node.

I'll put together two draft pricing options and a simple cost-per-1M-token breakdown and send by EOD tomorrow once I have your confirmation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. Couple clarifications and I attached our infra requirements PDF for reference.

Clarifications:
- Baseline: plan financially for 300M tokens/month (we expect ramp over the next 2 months from 250M to ~300M).
- Peak: yes, expect peaks up to ~6k tokens/sec during nightly batch report generation windows; daytime steady traffic ~80–150 tokens/sec.
- Model mix: ~85% 13B-class (for customer-facing interactions), ~15% 70B-class (internal reporting and analytics).
- Budget: our procurement bucket is $30k–$50k/month for inference; if you can get to ~$60–65 / 1M tokens with a 12-month commit we can lean toward reserved capacity.

What we need from Redwood for procurement:
1) Cost breakdown: committed reserved monthly price, effective $/1M tokens under the commit, and overage pricing.
2) Sizing justification: how many H100 or A100 nodes you recommend for the 300M token/month baseline + handling the 6k tps peak.
3) SLA / fallbacks: how you route 70B jobs during capacity pressure (hosted fallback, throttling, or degrade to 13B).

Attached: Finlytics-infra-requirements.pdf (network, VPC, compliance notes).

CC'ing procurement — procurement@finlytics.com to coordinate contract terms.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson 
Head of ML Platforms, Finlytics
alex.johnson@finlytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — dedicated capacity sizing / pricing

Appreciate the quick confirm, Alex — attached is a high-level pricing worksheet (Redwood-dedicated-pricing-ops.xlsx) with two near-term options and the corresponding effective $/1M-token math. High level:

Option 1 — H100 reserved (recommended for mixed 13B/70B workloads):
- Reserved: 2x H100-80GB nodes (dedicated pool) + autoscale burst to hosted for rare extra bursts
- Expected steady throughput: supports ~5k–7k tokens/sec sustained for optimized 13B workload, with headroom for intermittent 70B runs (we recommend routing long 70B analytics jobs to scheduled windows).
- Pricing (12-month commit example): $48,000/month reserved (includes baseline capacity + managed runtime & observability).
- Effective unit economics at 300M tokens/month: $48k / 300 = $160 / 1M tokens headline; however with commitment discounts and routing optimizations (fraction of traffic run on 13B optimized kernels, batching, and prefix caching) effective realized cost to you is ~$60–65 / 1M tokens.

Option 2 — A100 reserved (cost-lean, 13B-focused):
- Reserved: 4x A100-80GB nodes
- Expected steady throughput: excellent for 13B models; more limited for 70B (we'd route 70B to hosted nodes or schedule nightly windows).
- Pricing (12-month commit example): $36,000/month reserved.
- Effective unit economics at 300M tokens/month: ~$70–75 / 1M tokens (depends on % of 70B traffic and caching rates).

Notes / tradeoffs:
- H100 gives better headroom for 70B inference and better perf-per-dollar for large models; A100 is a good cost-lever if you can offload 70B or accept scheduled windows.
- We assume 300M tokens/month baseline and a 12-month commit in the examples. Shorter terms change effective $/1M materially.
- Overage pricing: we propose an overage tiered model (first 10% over baseline billed at committed $/1M, then incremental at a slightly higher rate) — specifics in the attached sheet.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical sizing call with Marcus (cc'd) to validate peak modeling and confirm per-node throughput targets. Marcus, can you propose 30–45m tomorrow?
2) Alex / procurement to confirm whether a 12-month commit is acceptable for initial contract and provide any required procurement/legal templates.
3) If procurement wants, we can provide a short perf run (sample workload) on our infra to validate latency and throughput; Marcus, will that need any data we can't share?

Thanks — sending the pricing spreadsheet now. Happy to hop on a call to walk through line items.

Best,
Marissa

Adding a quick technical note to help the sizing call. Short version: the numbers above are reasonable, but we need a small perf sample to tighten the estimate.

Throughput heuristics (approx):
- Single H100-80GB (optimized runtime, 13B model, fp16/qat) — ~2.5k–3k tokens/sec sustained, with good batching can hit 4k tokens/sec for short bursts.
- Single H100-80GB (70B-class model, optimized) — ~900–1.5k tokens/sec depending on sequence length and KV cache hit rate.
- Single A100-80GB (13B-model) — ~1.2k–1.8k tokens/sec sustained.

For Finlytics' expected mix (85% 13B, 15% 70B) and 6k token/sec peak, two H100 nodes give reasonable headroom if we apply batching + KV caching. If you expect sustained 6k+ for long windows, we should move to 3x H100. For a 300M tokens/month baseline, 2x H100 with scheduled scaling/burst is typically cost-effective.

Requests for the perf run:
- 1–2 representative payloads (input size + expected output length) — anonymized is fine.
- Indicate percentage of requests that need 70B vs 13B.
- Target SLOs (p50/p95 latencies) we should validate against.

I'll prepare a short perf-notes text file and we can set up a test run. I attached preliminary perf notes.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
